t.4.13.1: From Ṛśyamūka, that righteous-souled elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa went, together with Sugrīva, to Kiṣkindhā, which was guarded by the valour of Vālin.
t.4.13.2: Rāma, raising his great bow adorned with gold and taking up arrows that shone like the sun and brought victory in battle,
t.4.13.3: Ahead of that great-souled Rāghava went the thick-necked Sugrīva and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa.
t.4.13.4: Behind them came the heroic Hanumān, Nala and the monkey Nīla, and the greatly splendid Tāra, chiefs of the leaders of the monkey troops.
t.4.13.5: Gazing upon the trees bowed down under the weight of their blossoms, and upon the rivers bearing clear waters as they flowed onward to the sea, they went on their way.
t.4.13.6: They beheld valleys and mountains, clefts and caves as well, the foremost peaks, and ravines pleasing to behold.
t.4.13.7: Along the way they also saw ponds full of water, adorned with leaves as spotless as beryl and with lotuses whose buds rose toward the sky.
t.4.13.8: They saw the lakes echoing with the cries of kāraṇḍa ducks, sārasa cranes, haṃsas, vañjula birds and waterfowl, and likewise of cakravākas and other birds.
t.4.13.9: On every side they saw deer, fearless roamers of the forest, feeding on tender shoots of grass, some wandering about and others standing on the open grounds.
t.4.13.10: And they saw too the wild elephants, fearsome, roaming alone, adorned with white tusks, foes of ponds and breakers of riverbanks.
t.4.13.11: Those who were under Sugrīva's command went swiftly through the forest, beholding other forest-dwelling creatures and birds that roam the sky.
t.4.13.12: As they were going swiftly there, Rāma, the delight of the Raghus, seeing a forest thick with clusters of trees, spoke to Sugrīva.
t.4.13.13: This grove of trees shines like a cloud in the sky, vast as a mass of clouds and encircled at its edges by plantain trees.
t.4.13.14: What is this? I wish to know, my friend, for I am curious. I wish to have my curiosity dispelled by you.
t.4.13.15: Having heard those words of the great-souled Rāghava, Sugrīva, even as he went on walking, then described that great forest.
t.4.13.17: Here there lived seven sages known as the Saptajanas, firm in their vows, seven of them, who constantly lay in the water with their heads turned downward.
t.4.13.16: This, O Rāghava, is a vast hermitage that dispels weariness, rich in gardens and groves, with sweet roots, fruits and water.
t.4.13.18: These forest-dwellers, taking their only meal once every seven nights, and that of air alone, ascended to heaven in their very bodies after seven hundred years.
t.4.13.19: Thus, by their power, the āśrama, enclosed by a rampart of trees, is utterly unassailable even by the suras and asuras together with Indra.
t.4.13.20: Birds avoid this place, and so do the other creatures that roam the forest. Even those who enter here out of delusion never return again.
t.4.13.22: The three sacred fires, too, are blazing, for this smoke is seen, dense and reddish like a dove's body, as if enveloping the treetops.
t.4.13.21: Here, O Rāghava, the jingling of ornaments is heard, along with voices clear in every syllable, the sounds of musical instruments and songs, and a divine fragrance as well.
t.4.13.23: "O righteous-souled one, offer your salutation, directing it toward them." Then Rāghava, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, self-restrained and with palms reverently joined, did so.
t.4.13.24: For those who bow down to those sages of purified souls, O Rāma, no inauspiciousness whatsoever is seen in their bodies.
t.4.13.26: Having paid their respects, the righteous Rāma, his brother Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva and the monkeys went on their way with joyful hearts.
t.4.13.25: Then Rāma, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, the two great-souled ones, joined his palms in reverence and, turning his thoughts toward those sages, respectfully saluted them.
t.4.13.27: Having traveled a long way from that hermitage of the Seven Sages, they beheld Kiṣkindhā, the unassailable city guarded by Vālin.
